newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sandinistas storm out of Nicaraguan parliament.
newsitem.headline: Sandinistas storm out of Nicaraguan parliament.

text.p: Legislators of the left-wing Sandinista Front stormed out of Nicaragua's National Assembly late on Thursday, vowing to take their protests to the streets after election authorities rejected a Sandinista proposal.

In the new National Assembly's first session, 36 Sandinista legislators left the 93-member assembly to protest a Supreme Electoral Council (CSE) decision to make the vote for the assembly's president and board of directors public, instead of secret as the Sandinistas had demanded.

"We are not going to be complices in a process that is affecting the legitimacy, the legality, the constitutional order and the rule of law," the head of the Sandinista bench, Daniel Ortega, said before storming out of the building.

The Sandinistas wanted the vote secret because they said third-party legislators would be afraid to vote for Sandinista-sponsored candidates and risk the wrath of the new right-wing government of Arnoldo Aleman.
Aleman will be sworn in as president on Friday.

Despite the withdrawal of the opposition legislators, representatives of Aleman's Liberal Alliance and their allies elected Liberal congressman Ivan Escobar Fornos president of the National Assembly. In addition, pro-Liberal candidates were elected to the board of director's six other posts.

As they left the building, Sandinista legislators said they would take their protests to the streets since parliament, the government and the judiciary were all now in the hands of Aleman, and warned of an impending Liberal dictatorship.
"Here, any law that Aleman does not like will have little possibility of being passed," Victor Hugo Tinoco, second to Ortega in the Sandinista delegtion, told reporters.
"The people will have to settle their problems in the streets. Nicaragua is nearing a dictatorship; it is nearing a response from the people to the methods of a dictatorship," he said.
The Sandinistas have a history of revolutionary militancy and often used their muscle to frustrate the early years of the outgoing government of President Violeta Chamorro.
